name: Reach / target / likely label
what: Each college gets a label from a written rule in code, from its published admit rate and middle score range. Never from a model.
where: The counters on the first view; "Why this label" tab on each college, with the rule, its inputs and what was not used.

name: On the edge, and publishers disagree
what: Every label is rerun with the score 30 points either way and the admit rate 5 points lower; a label that flips is marked. Five published rulebooks are run on the same score and any disagreement is shown.
where: "on the edge" under a college in the picture; the "Why this label" tab.

name: Cases like this student, two pools
what: Counts of admitted, denied and waitlisted among finished cases like this student, with n, the matching rules used, examples, and the official admit rate beside them. The school's own verified cases and the national self-reported pool are never added together.
where: "Cases like this student" tab.

name: What the college says it weighs
what: Statements from each college's own Common Data Set form, each with its field, year and source link, checked in code and confirmed against a knowledge base. Common beliefs are checked against the form.
where: "What the college says" tab; lever 3 on the first view.

name: List balance and suggested fills
what: Warnings when a list is reach-heavy, has no likely or no target, piles onto very selective colleges, or is short. Up to six suggested colleges that would be likely or target, preferring the home state.
where: The one warning beside the counters; lever 1, "Show suggested colleges".

name: "What if the score were…" slider
what: Moves the student's score and re-labels the whole list as it moves, with a ladder of which colleges change at which score. Labels only; nothing else is re-run.
where: Lever 2 on the first view.

name: Where this student stands
what: One picture: every college's middle score range on a shared score line, the student's score drawn through them, admits-of-10 dots and case dots per college.
where: The first view, "Score ranges".

name: Essay notes with quotes, after masking
what: Names, addresses, phones and dates are masked, then one model reads the essay and returns observations with word-for-word quotes; code drops any note whose quote is not in the essay. A second model tags the major independently. An essay with instructions aimed at an AI is stopped twice.
where: "Essay notes" in the footer; the stopped banner.

name: How this was made: the five steps
what: Retrieve, score, bucket, explain, log: what each step did, how long it took, and whether code or a model did it. Sentences hidden by checks are counted with the reason.
where: "How this was made" in the footer.

name: Add a finished case
what: A counselor records a finished case for the school's own pool. Anything that looks like a name, email, phone or date of birth is refused.
where: "Add a finished case" in the footer.

name: One-page sheet for the family
what: A print layout with the list by label, the balance warnings, suggested colleges, and the caveats, in plain words.
where: "Print for the family" in the footer.

name: No personal chance of admission
what: The screen never shows a percentage for the student. Asking for one gets an explanation and a pointer to the evidence instead.
where: "What is the student's chance?" in the footer; every count sits beside the official admit rate.

name: Shared preview with no server
what: Saved runs for the six demo students, with the what-if scores, as plain files that open from a folder or a zip.
where: python tools/make_static.py --zip

name: Closeness: admitted or denied, which does the student resemble?
what: Per college, the distance from the student to the 7 nearest admitted and the 7 nearest denied cases, over score, activities rating, major group, hooks and residency. A lean, a steady test, the parts that are close or far, and the nearest cases. A distance, never a percentage; the label is untouched.
where: "Who they resemble" tab on each college.

name: Rings picture
what: The student at the centre, one dot per college as far out as the student is from the people admitted there. Hollow when there are too few cases; on an outer ring when it cannot be placed.
where: The first view, "Rings".

name: Mind map picture
what: The student in the middle, a branch per label, a node per college, and under each college its nearest kind of admitted student and its three nearest admitted cases.
where: The first view, "Mind map".

name: Scatter, part bars, kinds and changes
what: A scatter of that college's cases by score and activities rating with the student as a star and the three kinds' medoids ringed; a bar per part; three kinds of admitted student found by k-medoids and named from counts; and what would bring the student closer (score, activities, a named major; never hooks, home state or GPA).
where: "Who they resemble" tab.

name: Activities rating input
what: A 0 to 10 dial for the counselor's own rating of the student's activities, used only by closeness.
where: Edit details, "Activities, your rating".

name: Holds-up check for closeness
what: 400 past posters, each hidden in turn, their lean computed and their real outcome counted. Shown as counts with the caveat about self-reporting.
where: "How this was made", bottom; python -m engine.similarity --check

name: About, and How it was built
what: A tour with live buttons; the parts and weights, the algorithm as a diagram, the libraries, the choices made, every data source with what was taken from it, and this feature list. Weights and thresholds are read from the engine, not typed into the page.
where: The two links in the header; the feature list is at the end of How it was built.

name: Tests and the acceptance sheet
what: 216 unit tests with no network, including one that fails if the fixture or this feature list drifts from its copies. 60 labels worked out by hand from the published rows, by a builder who did not see the label code: 60 of 60 match.
where: python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . ; python tests/acceptance/run_acceptance.py

name: PRISM Evaluator on the essay notes
what: The run's score is read back in code instead.

name: Several intended majors in the form
what: Closeness can try another major the student named, but the form sends only one; the API accepts major_interests.

name: Matching on essay and activity text
what: The public case file has no essay text, so essay themes only reorder the school's own cases and closeness never reads text.
